newsitem.title: FRANCE: France suspends contacts with Bosnia envoys.
newsitem.headline: France suspends contacts with Bosnia envoys.

text.p: France on Monday became the second country to suspend contacts with Bosnia's envoys abroad in order to exert pressure on Bosnia's factions to settle a dispute over distribution of ambassadorial posts.

Foreign Ministry spokesman Yves Doutriaux announced the action by Paris after the international community's High Representative Carlos Westendorp recommended to Western powers that no ambassador be treated as a legitimate representative of Bosnia until a law governing the appointments was agreed.
"This measure aims to ensure that the ambassadors of Bosnia-Herzegovina represent a single government and will speak on behalf of all three Bosnian communities," Doutriaux told a daily news briefing.

"Consequently, we urge the Presidents (Alija) Izetbegovic, (Kresimir) Zubak and (Momcilo) Krajisnik to fully assume their responsibilities and quickly reach a definitive agreement on this issue," he added.
Germany on Sunday became the first Western country to declare a suspension of contacts with Bosnia's envoys.

At a NATO summit in May, Western allies had threatened to impose penalties on the joint postwar government of Bosnia unless factions settled differences by August 1 over division of ambassadorial posts among Serbs, Croats, Moslems and others and reached agreements on laws governing citizenship and passports.
Westendorp had extended the deadline until Monday because good progress had been made on the laws governing citizenship and passports.
